ca7952fd19294e4ddc87647dc371d85797a42828.summary: Check Point Research reports that the May 2025 takedown of the Lumma infostealer, announced by Europol, the FBI and Microsoft, disrupted the malware but did not permanently remove it. The developer claims almost 2,500 domains were seized and services are restored. Russia-registered servers were reportedly not disabled, and stolen Lumma logs still sell online. The report says reputational damage will matter more than technology for recovery. Lumma was also observed in use by Scattered Spider, Angry Likho and CoralRaider.

hedges: The takedown likely did not permanently affect most of the Russia-hosted infrastructure, according to the report.
The report says the key factor for Lumma resuming activity will be reputational rather than technological.
Forum opinions are mixed: some think the operation will shut Lumma down or take it private, others think it will have no lasting effect.
Several takedown details come from the reports or from the Lumma developer's own account, not independent confirmation.
The planted webcam script is described as allegedly taking photos; threat actors claim the code is basic and would not execute properly.
The developer says customers' IP addresses were not logged; this is the developer's claim as reported.
